# nacatamalon

> A 2D and 3D game engine for the web, in TypeScript, on WebGPU with a WebGL2 fallback, aimed at
> the look of the consoles from the SNES to the GameCube. A scene is a function; it asks for what it
> needs with hooks, and what it creates is plain data you change.

This is the short guide. `llms-full.txt`, next to this file, is the full reference: every export
with its signature and documentation, each under a `### name` heading. Search it for any name below.

Worked examples, one per feature with all their code: https://nacatamalon.com/llms/examples.md lists
them by topic, each with an id, and `https://nacatamalon.com/llms/examples/<id>.md` is one of them.

## The mental model

- A **scene** is a function that runs **once**, when the scene starts. It creates things and
  registers what happens later, then returns `createScene()`.
- **Hooks** (`use*`) work only while a scene, or something spawned with `useSpawn`, is being built.
  Call them at the top of the function and keep what they return.
- **`create*` returns plain data.** Change its fields and the next frame shows it:
  `sprite.transform.x += 1`, `sprite.tint = getColor('red')`, `text.text = 'SCORE 10'`.
- **`useUpdate((delta, time) => { ... })`** runs every frame. `delta` is seconds since the last frame,
  capped at 0.25; `time` is seconds since the scene started.
- What acts on a thing is a function that takes it first: `destroy(sprite)`. What a hook returns is a
  handle with methods: `keys.isDown('ArrowLeft')`, `useScene().change('Level')`.
- Files load in the background. `useLoadTexture` and the other loaders return at once, and what uses
  the file appears when it arrives. `useLoader()` reports progress.

## A whole game

```ts
import { createGame, createScene, createSprite, createText, getColor, useKeyboard, useUpdate } from 'nacatamalon';

const Game = () => {
    const keys = useKeyboard();
    const paddle = createSprite({ width: 64, height: 10, tint: getColor('#ff6b1a'), transform: { x: 240, y: 300 } });
    const score = createText({ text: 'SCORE 0', transform: { x: 8, y: 8 } });
    let points = 0;

    useUpdate((delta) => {
        if (keys.isDown('ArrowLeft')) {
            paddle.transform.x -= 340 * delta;
        }
        if (keys.isDown('ArrowRight')) {
            paddle.transform.x += 340 * delta;
        }
        // The anchor is the middle, so the paddle's edges are half its width away.
        const half = paddle.width / 2;
        paddle.transform.x = Math.min(Math.max(paddle.transform.x, half), 480 - half);
        if (keys.justPressed('Space')) {
            points += 10;
            score.text = 'SCORE ' + points;
        }
    });

    return createScene();
};

// The page needs <div id="app"></div>. The first scene in the object starts.
createGame('#app', { width: 480, height: 320, background: getColor('#12102b') })({ Game });
```

## Conventions

- **2D is pixels**, origin at the top-left of the game, y grows down. With no `useCamera2d`, `x`
  and `y` are positions on the screen. **3D is y-up**; give every 3D scene a `useCamera3d`.
- **Canvas size**: `createGame` `width` and `height` are the game's size, and by default (`scaling:
  'none'`) the canvas is shown at exactly that size; it does not fit the page. Pass `scaling:
  'integer'` (whole multiples, crisp pixel art) or `'contain'` (as large as fits).
- **Splash**: off unless asked for. `createGame` `splash: true` opens the published game with
  "Made with NacatamalOn" for under two seconds while the first scene loads behind it; it is
  skipped on `localhost` and in automated browsers, so development and tests never see it.
  `splash: 'always'` shows it there too.
- **Sprite anchor** defaults to the middle, `{ x: 0.5, y: 0.5 }`: `transform` places the centre.
  `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` places the top-left corner, `{ x: 0.5, y: 1 }` the feet.
- **Text anchor** defaults to the top-left corner, `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`. `{ x: 0.5, y: 0 }` centres it on
  `x`; `{ x: 1, y: 0 }` puts its right edge on `x` (a score at the right of the screen);
  `{ x: 0.5, y: 0.5 }` centres it both ways on the point.
- **Sprite size**: a sprite created with both `width` and `height` has them as numbers. A sprite
  sized by its picture (a `texture`, no `width`/`height`) has them `undefined` until the picture loads.
- **Keys** are `KeyboardEvent.key` names: letters lowercase (`'a'`), named keys as they are
  (`'ArrowLeft'`, `'Enter'`, `'Escape'`). The space bar is `'Space'`; `' '` also works.
- **Text** needs no font: `createText({ text })` uses the built-in 8 px font, which has lowercase,
  accents, ñ, ¿ and ¡. `style.fontSize` is the line height in pixels; multiples of 8 stay crisp. A
  font of your own, passed as `font`: `useLoadFont({ src: '/fonts/x.ttf' })` for a `.ttf`/`.woff`
  (sharp at any size; `fontSize` is the em size as in CSS; no `.otf` with cubic outlines or `.woff2`),
  or `useLoadBitmapFont({ json, atlas })` for a bitmap font (an image plus a JSON of glyph positions).
  A font loaded with a `key` in an earlier scene is named by it, `createText({ text, font: 'title' })`,
  with no loader in that scene.
- **Mouse look** (first person): `usePointer().lock()` captures the mouse, but only when called from
  a click or key press (`pointer.onDown(() => { void pointer.lock(); })`); then turn the camera with
  `movementX`/`movementY` from `onMove`, which keep changing while `screenX`/`screenY` do not.
  `isLocked()` turns `false` when the player presses Esc.
- **Colours** are `{ r, g, b, a }`, each 0 to 1. `getColor` takes `'#ff6b1a'`, `0xff6b1a`, a CSS
  name (`'red'`) or any CSS colour (`'rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)'`, `'hsl(30 100% 50%)'`).
  To blend two colours (a sky between dusk and night), `lerpColor(a, b, t)`.
- **Glows, flashes, beams of light**: `createSprite({ ..., blend: 'additive' })` adds its colour to
  what is behind instead of covering it, the same as additive particles.
- **Hiding a model**: `createModel(...)` returns an object with `visible`; set it any time, even
  before the file arrives (its pieces arrive hidden). No need to walk `parts`.
- **Particle effects that depend on the game** (dust the colour of the ground, a tint per level):
  write the effect in code, `createParticles({ effect: { kind: 'particles2d', emission: { rate: 30 },
  colorOverLife: [{ t: 0, color: lerpColor(a, b, t) }], texture: createPixelTexture(puff) } })`, with
  the fields of a `.particles` file; it is ready at once. Pass the same object to share one effect.
- **Angles** are radians.
- **Types** come from the same imports as the functions, all starting with `T`:
  `import type { TSprite, TText } from 'nacatamalon';`.
- **Scenes** are registered by name: `createGame(...)({ Title, Level })`, an object, not an array.
  `useScene().change('Level')` starts `Level` and stops the current scene: its objects are removed
  and its `useUpdate` stops. Changing back runs that scene's function again from the start, so
  anything kept in its local variables or `useData` starts over.
- **`change()` acts at once, but the frame it is called in finishes**: the code after it and the old
  scene's other `useUpdate` callbacks still run that one frame, then never again. `return` right
  after `change()` if the rest should not run. The new scene's first update is the next frame, so the
  key that caused the change is not a fresh `justPressed` there.
- **Pictures generated in code, instead of a `<canvas>`**: drawn art (characters, tiles, backgrounds)
  is made in a pixel-art editor and loaded with `useLoadTexture`. When a picture has to be *generated*
  instead (procedural variations, a placeholder, noise or a mask for a shader, a picture that changes
  while the game runs, or art made by an agent with no image editor), use `createPixels` and paint it
  with `fillRect`, `drawLine`, `fillCircle`, `fillEllipse`, `fillGradient`, `fillNoise`, `blitPixels`,
  `mapPixels`...; write on it with `drawText(pixels, 'MOTEL', x, y, { color, font?, fontSize?, anchor? })`
  (no font: the built-in one, needing nothing; a loaded font must have arrived, so in the scene that
  loads it draw inside `useWatch(..., [font])` then `updatePixelTexture`), rather than hand-making a
  pixel font. Then `createPixelTexture(pixels)` in the scene body gives a texture for `createSprite({ texture })`
  or `createMaterial({ texture })`. **Do not draw on a `<canvas>`** (`document.createElement('canvas')`,
  `getContext('2d')`, `getImageData`): it only exists in a browser, and the native runtime has no page;
  the pixels functions run everywhere. Paint on the picture again and `updatePixelTexture(texture,
  region)` shows it, at any time. A build script saves one as a file with `encodePng` from
  `nacatamalon/authoring`.
- **Processing a drawn picture in code**: to *show* a PNG, `useLoadTexture`. To *read or change* it
  first (a palette swap, a white hit silhouette, an outline, a collision mask, a level read from an
  image), `useLoadPixels({ src })`, decoded with no canvas; hand it to `createPixelTexture(loaded,
  (p) => swapColors(p, [[from, to]]))`, which returns at once and fills in when the file lands, painting
  on a copy. The loaded `pixels` are shared: read them (`getPixel`), never paint on them directly.
- **Data that outlives a scene** goes in a store, created once at module level:
  `const session = createGameStore({ key: 'session', state: { score: 0 } });`, then
  `session.set((s) => { s.score += 10; })` in one scene and `session.state.score` in the next.
  `key` is required and must be unique per game: two stores with one key warn, and the later replaces
  the earlier.

## Gotchas

- A hook called inside `useUpdate`, an event handler, a timeout or after `await` throws
  `[NacatamalOn] <hook>: call it inside a scene body...`. Create everything up front and change
  `visible`, or spawn things with `useSpawn`.
- Movement without `* delta` runs faster on screens with a higher refresh rate.
- `createGame` with no matching element throws: the page needs the element before the script runs.
- Physics is behind its own imports and is switched on once: `installPhysics2d()` from
  `nacatamalon/physics2d`, or `installPhysics3d()` from `nacatamalon/physics3d`. The physics engines
  are included in the package: there is nothing else to install.
- A `'static'` body never moves. Something that moves and pushes others (a platform, a moving peg) is
  `body: 'kinematic'`, moved with `setLinearVelocity` on its handle, which is
  `getPhysicsWorld2d()?.bodyOf(useSelf())` (or `getPhysicsWorld3d`) taken while the object is built.
  The handle's `setLayers(layer, collidesWith)` changes what it collides with, and its `destroy()`
  removes the body and keeps the object. `destroy(object)` removes the object's body too.

## Where things are (search llms-full.txt for each name)

- **Game and scenes**: `createGame`, `createScene`, `useScene`, `useGame`, `useSpawn`, `useSelf`, `destroy`, `useSceneUnmount`.
- **Time**: `useUpdate`, `useTimer`, `useTween`, easings such as `linear` and `easeInOutSine`.
- **Input**: `useKeyboard`, `usePointer`, `useGamepad`, `useActions`, `useAction`.
- **2D**: `createSprite`, `useLoadTexture`, `useLoadAtlas`, `useSpriteAnimation`, `createText`, `useLoadFont`, `useLoadBitmapFont`, `createNineSlice`, `createTilemap`, `tileAt`, `solidAt`, `createParticles`, `useCamera2d`.
- **3D**: `createMesh`, `useCubeGeometry`, `usePlaneGeometry`, `useUvSphereGeometry`, `createMaterial`, `useLoadGltf`, `createModel`, `useSkeletalAnimation`, `useCamera3d`, `cameraLookAt`, `useLight`, `usePointLight`, `useSpotLight`, `useBlobShadow`, `createParticles3d`.
- **Material maps** (extra pictures for a model's shader): `createMaterial({ shader: 'mesh3d', texture, maps: { noise, env }, fragment })` carries up to 4 named maps; the shader reads one with `sampleMap_<name>(uv)` (`sampleMap_noise(ctx.uv)`), and `envUv(ctx)` gives the coordinates of a chrome reflection (`sampleMap_env(envUv(ctx))`). A map the material lacks reads white. In the shader composer, `composerMapSample(name, uv)`, `composerEnvUv()` and `composerShine()` (prefer the composer: it writes both shader languages from one graph).
- **The 1997 look**: material options `vertexSnap` and `affine`, `useFog`, `usePostProcess` with `dither`, `posterize`, `paletteMatch`, `lutGrade`, `crt` (with `CRT_PRESETS`) and `COLOR_LEVELS`.
- **Screen effects** (each spread into `usePostProcess`, tuned by writing into `effect.uniforms`): `colorAdjust`, `mosaic`, `wave`, `shockwave`, `distort`, `rgbSplit`, `glitch`, `grain`, `oldFilm`, `halftone`, `blur`, `zoomBlur`, `motionBlur`, `tiltShift`, `bloom`, `godrays`, `phosphor`, `ntsc`, `lcd`. A hand-written effect can read `sampleTextureSmooth`, `sampleInput` and `sampleHistory`, and take `passes` for more than one read of the frame.
- **Pixels** (pictures painted in code): `createPixels`, `setPixel`, `getPixel`, `fillRect`, `drawLine`, `fillCircle`, `drawCircle`, `fillEllipse`, `drawEllipse`, `drawText`, `fillGradient`, `fillNoise`, `fillChecker`, `blitPixels`, `mapPixels`, `clonePixels`, `swapColors`, `createPixelTexture`, `updatePixelTexture`, `useLoadPixels`.
- **Audio**: `useSound`, `useMusic`, `useLoadAudio`, `useAudio`, `useAudioListener`.
- **State**: `useData`, `useWatch`, `createGameStore`, `useStore`, `createGameSignal`, `useSignal`.
- **Maths and random**: `useRandom`, `clamp`, `lerp`, `vec2Add`, `vec3Add` and the other `vec2*`/`vec3*`.
- **2D physics**: `installPhysics2d` from `nacatamalon/physics2d`; `usePhysicsWorld2d` and `usePhysicsBody2d` from `nacatamalon`.
- **3D physics**: `installPhysics3d` and `useCharacterBody` from `nacatamalon/physics3d`; `usePhysicsWorld3d` and `usePhysicsBody3d` from `nacatamalon`.
- **Saved scenes**: `sceneFromDoc`, `parseSceneDoc`.

`nacatamalon/authoring` and `nacatamalon/extend` are for tools and engine extensions; a game never needs them.
